prompt:
Use case: image-to-3D reconstruction reference. ONE isolated ruined stone castle, the crumbling remains of an ancient fortress, for a third-person fantasy adventure game. Isolated complete object on a plain medium grey studio background, elevated three-quarter frontal view from the front-left so the whole layout and every walkable floor is visible from above. Weathered pale grey limestone masonry, natural matte stone, moss-free, no vegetation. The ruin is VERY WIDE and LOW: roughly 80 metres wide, 60 metres deep and only about 14 metres tall, with exactly TWO storeys and no towers taller than the top floor. GROUND STOREY: a very broad flat stone forecourt enclosed by low broken crenellated outer walls, entered through one wide collapsed arch gate in the front wall, with fallen blocks scattered near the walls only, leaving the floor open. SECOND STOREY: an ENORMOUS ROOFLESS GREAT HALL that covers most of the footprint: one huge flat open stone floor, open to the sky, surrounded only by broken half-height walls, stumps of shattered columns along the edges and a few ruined pillars, with no roof, no ceiling, no upper towers. Essential focus: TWO EXTREMELY WIDE, LOW, GENTLE STONE STAIRCASES on the left and right of the forecourt, each at least 12 metres wide with broad regular shallow treads and no railings, rising directly and continuously from the forecourt floor to the great hall floor, plus one wide central grand stair between them; every stair lands on the hall floor with an unambiguous continuous walkable connection and no stair ends in a wall. Clean robust blocky architectural forms, readable silhouette, no tiny spires, no thin fragile arches, no detached floating parts, no moat, no landscape, no ground plane texture beyond the castle, no people, no creatures, no text, no labels, no watermark. Complete object framed with 10 percent margin, even neutral soft studio lighting, high fidelity stylized realistic game asset render. This is a broad two-level ruin with a gigantic open-air hall on top and very wide easy stairs, NOT a tall multi-towered intact castle.

Pale weathered grey limestone, slightly cool tone, crisp block edges, the hall floor clearly lighter than the walls.
